To detect mental patients on social media, many efforts have been taken to analyze individual posts using machine learning techniques. The purpose of this paper is to provide a systematic overview of studies in the mental disorder detection field. A comprehensive review on a list of datasets extracted from various social media platforms and a summary of the types of features explored in mental disorder detection are given in this paper. Also, different regular machine learning techniques and deep learning approaches used in previous studies are discussed. Several directions for future research are also presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Cybersecurity: A Review
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computing and Data Science (CDS)
abstract: With the development of Internet technology, the scale of Internet has increased considerably, which brings with a large number of cyber-attacks. Traditional protection techniques are confronted with complex, advanced and ongoing evolvement adversarial situations, which have to be more adaptive and responsive in order to handle future security and privacy problems. Deep Learning (DL), as one of the most currently remarkable machine learning techniques, has a great potential in cybersecurity. In this paper, author is committed to analyze current cyber-attacks, to review recent state-of-the-art deep learning algorithms and Figure out pros and cons of them, and to discuss the feasibility of deep learning technology applied to cybersecurity to defend malware attacks, DDoS attacks and spoofing attacks. This article also analyzes some vulnerabilities of deep learning algorithms and potential security problems which might come out when DL is applied to cybersecurity. Finally, paper discusses some challenges a DL-based defense mechanism has to overcome, and status and future directions of DL-based defense technology.

articleTitle: Securing Database Integrity in Intelligent Government Systems that Employ Fog Computing Technology
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computing and Data Science (CDS)
abstract: Phenomenal technological developments have an immense and broad impact on the future of adaptive and evolving government systems. Technologies, such as cloud computing, fog computing, and the Internet of Things (IoT), offer governments and their citizens opportunities to enhance their experiences and services; increased availability and higher-quality services via real-time data processing augment the potential for technology to add value to everyday experiences. This paper presents a novel model for an intelligent government system that uses fog computing technology to control and manage the data of the entire system. Guaranteeing trusted and reliable communication between entities is the primary intent of this model. Unique algorithms, focused on sustaining the system's data integrity in the event of a system attack, are proposed and evaluated.

articleTitle: An Improved SVR-FCM Method for Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Aircraft Engines
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computing and Data Science (CDS)
abstract: Predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) remains an important part in prognostics and health management (PHM) discipline. But the complexity of machine system and the noise in data make the prediction full of uncertainty and diversity. On the other hand, the traditional statistic methods are not capable for this kind of problems because of the limited number of data and previous knowledge. In this case, the machine learning methods are widely used in PHM field, since they are data-driven approaches which enable the model to determine the states without considering a homogeneous pattern. In this paper, the kernel principal component analysis and sliding window method are introduced for extracting the main features of the raw datasets. Then, support vector machine is used to predict the RUL of aircraft engines using data from C-MAPSS. The real RUL is uncertain, based on the value of features, so the fuzzy theory is introduced to the model to get the prediction interval of RUL. This paper also provides the performance running on dataset FDOOI to compare with prior approaches.

articleTitle: Object Detection for Automatic Driving Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computing and Data Science (CDS)
abstract: With the continuous developing progress of automatic driving, object detection is continuously being applied and developed. This paper presents an overview of deep learning object detection algorithm that used in the field of automatic driving. In the first part, we will introduce the research status and challenges of deep learning-based object detection in automatic driving. In the second part, we will introduce a deep learning-based object detection algorithm. Distinct algorithms will be discussed in the same structure. 1) Introduction 2) Algorithm steps 3) Advantages and Disadvantages. In the third part, we will compare different algorithms according to different principles. In the fourth part, we will introduce the practical application of deep learning-based object detection algorithm in the field of automatic driving.

articleTitle: A Data Analytics Study in the Influence of Top Universities over World-Class Cities Based on QS Best Cities Ranking
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computing and Data Science (CDS)
abstract: Attracting the best students to top world universities has become a social phenomenon that challenges host university cities in accommodating those students every year. This article presents an analysis of methodology developed by QS Best Student Cities Ranking, using a set of six variables and one goeal variable The goal is to provide students, parents and governors with a methodology that allows them to assess the quality of life in different cities of the world and how they can improve the experience of international students. We present a model for ranking Best Student Cities using QS Dataset with five years of data (2014-2019) and 120 cities. The model is built using data mining techniques that include correlation and multivariable panel data to find city trends in improving their position with respect to the six indicators established in the QS methodology. Our study reveals the impact that higher education influences on the public image of cities worldwide and provides a useful tool for city majors, students, and parents, granting them an insight on what higher education students seek to achieve a successful university experience.

articleTitle: An ITSM Framework Adaptation: Case Study in an Electoral Institution
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computing and Data Science (CDS)
abstract: This paper contributes to ITSM framework adaptations in IT service provider organizations, specifically in Local Electoral Public Institutions in Mexico. It also aims to provide a series of useful indicators and standardized operating procedures so an electoral IT department is capable of measuring its own performance and thus align its operation towards continuous improvement. An ITSM methodological adaptation of the Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL) is presented, it was conducted in four stages that started with establishing the mission and vision of the organization and concluded with developed framework; it included thirteen processes and seven activities which are used as an IT service provision and strategic alignment guide. Empirical analysis results confirm that adapting and implementing processes and knowledge tools, contribute to quality and user satisfaction when providing information technology services. The implementation of this methodology statistically demonstrated an 88% improvement in response times to incidents or service requests. This research is among the first attempts to develop an IT best practice framework adaptation for an electoral institution in Mexico that is leverageable to 32 likewise organizations across the country with the characteristics described in this paper. It also promotes the adaptation of existing management strategies from the literature to an organization.

articleTitle: A Survey Paper on Movie Trailer Genre Detection
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computing and Data Science (CDS)
abstract: Like a lot of movies are being made and their trailer videos are being uploaded on the internet and there are different types of algorithms and models that are used in detecting the genre of the movie genre. Here we have tried to implement the model and compare it with other models and suggest which model is better to implement. In most of the paper, the common genre which was used to detect were drama, action, thriller, and horror. But according to IMDb, there are 28 genres of videos. So still, there is a long way to go in this field.

articleTitle: Client Request Analysis Tool for CERN ALICE Grid Services
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computing and Data Science (CDS)
abstract: ALICE is an experiment hosted at the CERN facilities in Geneva. The data collected by the experiment is distributed in multiple geo-locations. ALICE software development team is managing the technologies that offer a unitary view to the distributed resources. AliEn API Services and JAliEn Services are used by the researchers to access and analyze the collected data. The ALICE developers cannot analyze the client-server interactions, while the only information available is gathered in the log files. The main requirement of the project is to provide an analysis tool to extract vital information out the log files. The tool is tested against log files generated by the ALICE production servers and is deployed on a custom ALICE-owned instance. As of June 2020, the project is being used by the developers to extract near real-time viable requests information and have a correct picture of the researcher's interaction with the services.

articleTitle: The Evaluation on the Development Potential of Rural Commercial Endowment Insurance in Guangdong Province under the Strategy of Rural Revitalization
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computing and Data Science (CDS)
abstract: With the rural Ageing Situation, based on the present situation of rural old-age security in Guangdong county, constructing the evaluation index of the development potential of rural commercial endowment Insurance, using factor analysis method, the development of rural commercial endowment Insurance is summarized into four factors: social development factor, economic development factor, natural condition factor, income level factor, calculating the comprehensive score and ranking of the development potential of commercial endowment insurance. By means of clustering analysis, the index similarity is divided into four categories in county rural areas of Guangdong Province. For different categories, relevant departments should adopt differentiation strategy to promote the development of commercial endowment insurance in Guangdong, promote rural revitalization according to local conditions.

articleTitle: A Summary and Analysis of Articles that Based on Studying Text Data and Digital Data
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computing and Data Science (CDS)
abstract: With the development of society and technology, the development of big data, the variety of processing, and the huge amount of data has become one of the core elements of people's lives. When people process certain data, they would like to find some conclusions to help them achieving new levels or expand the existing findings. Now, in addition to processing traditional digital data, text data can also be processed quickly. This article studies some articles based on big data, economics, business, etc. First of all, they are classified according to the type of data they study, and they are further summarized to draw some conclusions about behavior (like how to make a business decision, how to deal with the financial problems) and explanations of economic phenomena.

articleTitle: Detecting Overlapping Communities via Expanding Core Regions
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computing and Data Science (CDS)
abstract: A social circle usually has some cores. Inspired by this phenomenon, we consider that a community in a complex network is also formed around one or several core vertices, called core region. We define the core score of a vertex to reflect its ability to attract other vertices. Utilizing the core scores of vertices, we address how to find the core region of one community, and then we apply local expansion and optimization to detect communities based on these core regions. Besides detecting community structure, our method can detect some abnormal vertices that are the hubs of network. Experimental results based on artificial networks and real-world networks show that our method is more effective than some usual methods.

articleTitle: Obesity Rate, Economy Condition and Races: Exploration on Spatial Heterogeneity of Obesity- Related Factors Based on Geographical Weighted Regression (GWR) in City of Los Angeles
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computing and Data Science (CDS)
abstract: Obesity is a severe health problem in the world and obesity prevention in the United States is vital for the well-being of citizens and society as a whole. Goal of this research is to examine the correlation between adult obesity rate and economy condition and different races. It also explores the spatial heterogeneity of the impact of studied variables using geographic weighted regression (GWR) by census tract. Study area is city of Los Angeles where has diverse population and the income disparities. Results show that spatial distribution of adult obesity rate has significant clustering effect (Moran's I = 0.72). We also found high spatial heterogeneity in adult obesity rate and studied variables. Since at different locations, impacts of different races and economy condition varied greatly, this research can provide useful information for more targeted obesity prevention programs in city of Los Angeles in the future.

articleTitle: Ensemble Incremental Learning Iterative Mechanism on Reject Inference
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Computing and Data Science (CDS)
abstract: This paper investigates the possibility of using statistical methods (extrapolation and NB) and supervised learning algorithms (LightGBM, xgboost, RF, LR, catboost) to build a benchmark model through the Ensemble Learning (using Weighted Voting) to predict the default status of rejected samples and therefore obtain full sample data set. One challenge of this research is proposing a new training sample selection process, which requires an effective mechanism for rejecting the sample inclusion ratio and multiple rounds of iterative verification based on AUC. Based on the empirical analysis of the data sets of Xunmiao and Lendingclub, the results show that: reject inference can improve the prediction accuracy of the personal credit scoring model, and the improvement of accuracy is mainly due to the improvement of the correctness of the default customer.
